title: Applicability trigger — the applicability rule, v2 (D2)
description: PROPOSED in v2 Session 2. The 'trigger' of the session prompt is the rule that already exists in data/applicability.json (33 records, published on applies.html). A second entity would be a second home for the same facts, so v2 is that rule raised to the standard a claim meets (docs/ROADMAP-v2.md Phase 3 entry condition): every source reference carries `supports` and a locator, every condition resolves to a provision, every exemption and threshold names its basis. The matcher in js/applies.js reads `conditions` and `outcome` and is unchanged; every new field is evidence about the rule, not input to it. Rules T-01…T-11 in docs/V2-DATA-DESIGN.md §2.

x-prompt-mapping.domanda (question): The questionnaire dimensions the rule reads — the keys of `conditions` (actor, activity, territory). DERIVED as `asks`; the question wording keeps its one home in applies.html and js/applies.js and is not copied into each rule.
x-prompt-mapping.grado di certezza (certainty): `outcome` — applies / likely / possible / unlikely, with the meanings in data/applicability.json `$outcomes`. outcome:undetermined is never stored: only the engine emits it, for a combination no rule covers. `depends_on` states what the certainty turns on.
x-prompt-mapping.eccezioni/soglie (exceptions/thresholds): `exemptions` (v2: objects with an effect and a basis) and `conditions.thresholds` with `threshold_basis`.
x-prompt-mapping.rinvio con locator (reference with locat: `sources` (v2: reference objects with supports and locator, each saying what it is for) and `condition_provisions`.
x-prompt-mapping.verified_at: `last_verified`, as on every other record. No second date field.

for.description: What the reference establishes. `scope` = that the rule fires on these conditions (material, personal, territorial scope; the definition of an actor). At least one `scope` reference is required (T-02).

text.description: What the reader sees, as today.

effect.description: excludes: the instrument does not apply to the case (GDPR household exemption). narrows: some obligations fall away (DSA Art. 19). reinstates: an exception to an exception (DSA Art. 19(2), designation as a VLOP).

outside_dataset.description: true when the exemption sends the reader to an instrument this site has no record of (the Law Enforcement Directive in ap-gdpr-03). The text must then say so, as it does today.

instrument.description: An instrument id whose derived coverage is covered or mapped — never excluded (T-09).

conditions.description: UNCHANGED — the matcher's input. A dimension the rule omits is a wildcard. `thresholds` keys end in their comparator (_gt, _gte, _lt, _lte), and the comparator must be the one the legal text uses (T-05).

rationale.description: Editorial; the reading the rule encodes. Typed analytical content (docs/PROJECT-CONTEXT.md §4).

anyOf.description: v1 — accepted during migration; the rule is then not publishable at the v2 standard (T-04).

depends_on.description: The facts the outcome turns on and the questionnaire does not establish. Required non-empty for outcome:likely and outcome:possible (T-06).

anyOf.description: v1 bare ID — accepted during migration; such a rule is not publishable at the v2 standard (T-01).

condition_provisions.description: NEW. For each dimension the rule's conditions use, the provision IDs that define it. Every ID must be a provision record (validate.mjs already resolves provisions). This is the roadmap's 'every condition resolves to a provision ID' (T-03).

threshold_basis.description: NEW. One entry per key of conditions.thresholds: the references that state the threshold and its comparator (T-05).

last_verified.description: Required. The date the rule was last read against its locators; never later than the as-of date (T-07).

verification_note.description: NEW, optional. What was read and what was not, as on every other record.

x-derived.asks: The keys of `conditions` other than thresholds: which questionnaire questions the rule reads.
x-derived.publishable: true when T-01…T-05 hold. A rule that is not publishable is either not shown or shown as not yet verified to the claims' standard — the choice is decision D-2, which is the author's and is still open. Never stored: a rule becomes publishable by being read, not by being flagged.
x-derived.status_label: The rule's instrument's label (status-labels.json), shown with the outcome, so that a rule for an instrument in transition says so.
